overview:
Dr. Rui Lu received his Ph.D. degree from the University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and then completed his post-doctoral training at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. Dr. Lu’s laboratory is dedicated to uncovering the epigenetic mechanisms that drive cancer development, with the goal of developing targeted, mechanism-based therapies. His expertise spans transcriptional and epigenetic regulation, chromatin dynamics, and leukemia biology, honed through extensive molecular, cellular, genomic, mouse model, and bioinformatic approaches. His independent research programs in leukemia research have successfully attracted multiple competitive grants and have resulted in a series of high impact peer-reviewed papers (Cancer Cell 2016, Nature 2018, eLife 2020, Blood Advances 2021, Leukemia 2022, Blood 2024).

Currently, his lab is focused on understanding epigenetic regulation in hematological malignancies such as acute myeloid leukemia. Dr. Lu’s research covers three key areas: (1) investigating the molecular basis of driver mutations in cancer, (2) identifying novel targets for cancer epigenetic therapies, and (3) exploring the mechanisms of resistance to epigenetic therapies in cancer. Explore opportunities to join Dr. Lu's research at: https://www.lu-lab.org/joinus.
